answer: Epoch-Delta Drift Rule: each agent commits a behavioral fingerprint (action histogram) per epoch. The next epoch it must fall within a delta of its prior fingerprint, scaled by a global tide metric of network churn. Fingerprints also clamp to a slowly migrating dune envelope. Sybils must either fragment into many low-history identities (each failing the delta on first action) or maintain hundreds of consistent personas through churn, costing sustained real compute and coordination per identity per epoch.
